St. Philip the Evangelist and Deacon

St. Philip the Evangelist and Deacon

St. Philip the Deacon · St. Philip the Evangelist · St. Philip of the Seventy

Period
First century; precise lifespan not established here
Region
Jerusalem; Samaria; Caesarea; received ministry in Asia Minor
Titles / vocation
Apostle of the Seventy · Deacon · Evangelist
Commemoration
October 11

Introduction

St. Philip, one of the Seven, preaches in Samaria and explains Isaiah to the Ethiopian official in Acts. He is distinct from St. Philip of the Twelve.

Read the published life [1]

Death / martyrdom

Death in old age in the received OCA life

Read circumstances and sources

One of the Seven

Acts names St. Philip among the seven chosen when the Jerusalem community addresses the distribution of food to widows. He later becomes a preacher in Samaria after persecution disperses the believers. His identity is distinct from the Apostle of the Twelve with the same name.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Acts 6:1–6; 8:1–13

Teaching and baptism in Acts

On the road toward Gaza, he approaches an Ethiopian official who is reading Isaiah. Asked about the passage, St. Philip explains Jesus from the text and baptizes the official. Acts later places him at Caesarea, calls him the evangelist and one of the Seven, and mentions his four daughters who prophesy.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Acts 8:26–40; 21:8–9

Later received life

The OCA’s received account says that St. Philip later served as bishop in Tralles in Asia Minor and died in old age. Those details are distinguished from the canonical Acts narrative. The account does not describe his death as martyrdom.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Final paragraph on later ministry and death

Commemoration and identity

The OCA commemorates him on October 11 as an Apostle of the Seventy and one of the Seven Deacons. Its opening sentence expressly distinguishes him from St. Philip of the Twelve, whose commemoration is November 14.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Title, date and opening identity distinction
